plan.estimand: Superiority test of two-sided cluster-rate comparison (treatment rate 0.005 vs control rate 0.010 per child-week) with cluster-level coefficient-of-variation inflation
plan.hypothesis: H0: λ_treatment = λ_control = 0.010 per child-week vs H1: λ_treatment ≠ λ_control under cluster rate model with CV inflation
assumptions: Poisson rate model for events within clusters
Between-cluster variation modeled via coefficient-of-variation (CV) = 0.15 for rate heterogeneity
Additive one-cluster correction applied to variance inflation
Equal allocation (1:1 randomization)
Two-sided Wald-type test with normal approximation
Fixed exposure of 2500 child-weeks per cluster
Rates are constant across clusters under null hypothesis
scientific_notes: The cluster-rate CV approximation inflates variance due to between-cluster heterogeneity in rates. The additive one-cluster correction adds 1 to the cluster count in variance calculation.
Treatment rate (0.005) is half the control rate (0.010), constituting the minimal clinically relevant difference.
With 2500 child-weeks per cluster, expected event counts are approximately 12.5 (treatment) and 25 (control) per cluster.
CV = 0.15 is moderate clustering; with additive correction, this impacts the effective design effect calculation.
